direct_handler_bypass_finding.summary: Removing the privileged bypass was not sufficient. saathi/tools/registry.py::execute_tool ended in a direct handler invocation for every tool classified LEGACY_BOUNDED, which executed outside the ExecutionGateway contract: no approval reference, no idempotency key, no gateway audit record.

measured_before.method: every registered handler replaced by a counting mock; one probe per tool class
measured_before.worst_case: classify_legacy_tool() defaults unmatched names to LEGACY_BOUNDED, so any newly registered handler became executable without review

measured_after.coverage: every registered tool name, every tool class, every legacy entry point, speaker match True | False | unknown

authority_flow.before: identity signal → Identity.ADMIN → human_approved=True and code_confirmed=True → privileged bypass → handler executed in-process
authority_flow.after: identity signal → bounded metadata in the L7 audit only. Dispatcher runs as Identity.USER with human_approved=False and code_confirmed=False. Approval is only a server-minted ToolApprovalReference validated by ToolExecutionService. Execution is only via the canonical ExecutionGateway; everything else fails closed.

remaining_limitations: On-box callers are trusted. _is_local() treats a genuine loopback request with no forwarding header as authenticated, so any local process can reach the authenticated endpoints. This is pre-existing documented policy shared with /api/v1/agent/chat, not a change made here, and it is why the browser certificate models a remote caller through the proxy header.
/api/v1/voice/command still exists. It is authenticated, scoped, bounded and advisory, but it remains a legacy surface; retiring it entirely is future work.

Session scoping is single-owner. The deployment has one owner identity, so the principal namespace prevents cross-session access rather than cross-tenant access. Multi-tenant workspace binding is not implemented on this legacy path.

SaathiOS guards routes per page, not with a global shell guard. /settings/voice renders signed out; it exposes no enrollment and no server data, and the API refuses unauthenticated callers, but frontend route protection is not uniform.
The speaker match is still computed on an authenticated voice turn. It is metadata only and gates nothing, but the voiceprint code path has not been deleted.
The retired enrollment endpoint is retained as a truthful 410 rather than removed from the routing table, so old clients get an answer instead of a 404.
Advisory model output is unchanged. The model can still describe a privileged action; it simply cannot cause one through this path.
canonical_promotion_requirement: This repair lives in the SaathiAI-trunk-v3 worktree on an unpushed validation branch. The vulnerable main tree at ~/SaathiAI is unchanged. No LaunchAgent may be restored, and no production loopback stack may be restarted from ~/SaathiAI, until the repaired checkout is promoted to canonical and the LaunchAgent's target is reviewed against it.
